The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed
Why, in plain words: An admin switched on a new feature that sent shoppers' account pages through a monthly spending calculation, and that calculation likely fails for anyone who has bought nothing so far this month.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 11m 13s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 36.0% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): at least 7,545.67 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - refuted, put back when it did not help
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #576 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 12, 2026, 18:15 UTC, not back to normal by 18:26:13 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 8 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 18:28:02 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 18:22:02 UTC
Ended by: Argus: escalated to a person, Nov 12, 2026, 18:26:13 UTC - PR #576, opened as a draft

Summary
The service broke at 18:15 UTC and was not back to normal by 18:26:13 UTC, at least 11 minutes 13 seconds later. 30.5% of requests failed while it was broken, against 0.9% before it began. At its worst, 36.0% failed. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by at least 7,545.67 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. An admin switched on a new feature that sent shoppers' account pages through a monthly spending calculation, and that calculation likely fails for anyone who has bought nothing so far this month. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - refuted, put back when it did not help. On an earlier incident like this one, Argus had also reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature, and it was refuted there. Argus handed the incident to a person. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #576, for a person to review and merge. With monthly-spend-feature back on, account pages could keep failing for every shopper who has bought nothing this month, and switching the flag off in the flag provider might again not change what io-shop evaluates.

Impact
at least 11m 13s - since onset, still not back to normal
36.0% - peak error rate
4,398 - requests failed
0.9% to 30.5% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
at least 7,545.67 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
The monthly path that monthly-spend-feature switches on works out a shopper's average spend per item this month by dividing the month's total by the number of purchases made this month. Nothing guards against that number being zero, so for every shopper who has bought before but not this month, line 47 of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py raises ZeroDivisionError and the account page request fails. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed with server errors, starting in the onset minute and continuing through the last minute read.
  Evidence:
    T4 18:22:05 Investigator Agent: Read back 361 minutes of metrics
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 33 occurrences in 40 minutes, 17:46–18:25; # was 0.50% to 36.00%, typically 1.50%, highest at 18:21. After Argus first acted, logged in 18:23–18:25
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 22 occurrences in 11 minutes, 18:15–18:25. After Argus first acted, logged in 18:23–18:25
why 1 The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. These errors appear in io-shop's logs from the onset minute onwards and not before it.
  Evidence:
    G5309
why 2 An admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at 18:15:47 UTC. In that same minute, flag evaluations started moving from off to on, and from the next minute every evaluation came back on, which sent account page requests down the flag's monthly path.
  Evidence:
    P1 18:15:47 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 149 / on 51 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 18:15
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 10 occurrences in 10 minutes, 18:16–18:25. After Argus first acted, logged in 18:23–18:25
  Ruled out:
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 18 hours 25 minutes before 18:25; the Investigator Agent read back 2 production changes.
      T25
      T26
    The revision running on every replica, which the history does not name. With it in place and the flag off, account pages rendered normally and the flag evaluated off in every minute read before the onset.
      T30 18:25:07 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
      Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 8 occurrences in 30 minutes, 17:45–18:14
      G7e5d INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 17:45–18:14
why 3 The monthly path likely divides by the number of purchases made this month, which is zero for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
Contributing factors
- No check was seen that exercised the monthly path behind monthly-spend-feature for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on in production. By Code-Fix's reading, the tests in the file it read did not cover that case. (AI-2)
- No staged rollout of the flag was seen. From the minute after it was switched on, every evaluation of monthly-spend-feature in io-shop came back on. (AI-3)
- The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it. (AI-4)
- Switching monthly-spend-feature off in the flag provider did not change what io-shop evaluated: its logs kept showing the flag on after it was switched off. (AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 18:15:47 UTC. Account page requests that evaluate it then fail with ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate rose from about 1% to about 30%. No deployment or config change was recorded. | 0.95 | refuted
C2 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 18:15:47 UTC. Evaluations then moved from off to on, and account page requests started failing with a ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. The error rate went from about 1% to about 30%. No deployment is recorded, and the 3 replicas are converged. Latency, memory and CPU stayed flat. Argus switched the flag back off at 18:22:13 UTC, but the logs still showed it on and errors continued through 18:25. | 0.88 | refuted, as tested for C1

Trigger
No trigger was established.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 18:22:14 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | refuted, put back when it did not help
 | 18:26:13 | Proposed a fix: PR #576 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 18:15 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 18:22 UTC, 7 minutes later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #576 | open
AI-2 | Before a feature flag can be switched on in production, require tests that exercise the code path it enables, including edge cases such as a shopper with no purchases this month. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Roll out io-shop feature flags to a small share of requests first, and stop the rollout automatically when the error rate rises. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so that a person is paged when it fires. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Alert when the flag state io-shop logs that it evaluates disagrees with the flag provider's state after a flag change. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Switch monthly-spend-feature off again in a way that reaches every io-shop replica. Confirm at the service that io-shop's logs show the flag evaluating off, that the ZeroDivisionError lines from src/io_shop/spend_summary.py stop, and that the error rate falls back to about 0.9%. Keep it in place until the fault is fixed. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Find out why io-shop kept evaluating monthly-spend-feature as on after it was switched off in the flag provider at 18:22:13 UTC: whether the change reached the replicas at all, or was held back by caching, polling or another source of flag values. If it did reach them, find out why account pages kept failing. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-8 | Before the Mitigation Agent judges a change it made, have it confirm from the service's own logs that the change reached the service. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came 6 minutes after its series passed its line, within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute its series is read in.
- 5 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at 18:15.
- 13 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 14 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF.
- 3 minutes 2 seconds after the alert was raised, monthly-spend-feature was put back ON.
- 3 minutes 17 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C2.
- 4 minutes 13 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #576.
What went wrong
- C2 was marked refuted because of the test run for C1, even though C2 itself said that switching the flag off had not reached the service. The one action taken never got account pages off the monthly path, so it could not show whether the flag was the cause, and Argus moved on with no explanation left to try.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault is in average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. It divides account.total_this_month_cents by the number of purchases flagged in_current_month. When a shopper has bought nothing this month, that number is zero, and line 47 raises ZeroDivisionError. Plenty of shoppers have bought before but not this month (the test file's own helper calls this "the ordinary case"). So every request that render_spend_summary sent down the monthly path (use_monthly_summary=True) for such a shopper failed at the account-page boundary. Turning on monthly-spend-feature did not create the fault. It started sending requests to code that had always crashed on this input.

The fix: when nothing was bought this month, the function now returns 0, because a shopper with no purchases this month has spent 0 this month. For any month with at least one purchase it divides exactly as before. The lifetime figure (average_spend_per_item) is unchanged, so its existing test still expects ZeroDivisionError for an account that has never bought anything while the flag is off. The function's return type is still int, so account_page._the_figure_for and the rest of the page get the same kind of value as before.

Tests added to tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py:
• one calls average_spend_per_item_this_month directly, for a shopper with past purchases but none this month, and expects 0;
• one goes through render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True) and expects the same.

With the code as it stood, both would raise ZeroDivisionError.

Not addressed: the investigation reports the flag still evaluating "on" after it was switched off. Nothing I read in this repository evaluates or caches that flag (rollout.py holds only a share constant), so I made no change for it. With this fix, an "on" evaluation for such a shopper no longer fails.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-12
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

The document, by field:
overview: Some shoppers on io-shop could not load their account pages, and the problem lasted {duration}. An admin had switched on a new feature that sent shoppers' account pages through a monthly spending calculation, and that calculation likely fails for shoppers who have bought nothing so far this month. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. No one was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one. Argus switched the new feature off, but that did not help, so the feature was switched back on. Argus has also proposed a fix. It is open as a draft and has not been put in place yet.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
